summary: Charles Norman Seddon was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1889–1891) and served as Reader in Persian and Marathi at the University of Oxford from 1924.
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College, Oxford (c. 1878–1882) and held a post at the University of Oxford from c. 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (c. 1882–1886), later holding a post at SOAS University of London from c. 1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist who studied under traditional teachers and at East India Company College. He worked in the Indian Civil Service (1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at University College London (c. 1855–1879).
Charles Picard was an archaeologist and historian. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon from 1921 to 1934 and at the University of Paris from 1934 to 1955.

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Durham University and Oxford under Michael Aris, later serving as Professor at Oxford (2002–2005) and Director of Studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études from 2009.

Charles Rieu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Geneva and Bonn under Lassen, Freytag, and Gildemeister. He served at the British Museum, UCL as Professor of Arabic and Persian, and Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic.

Charles Robert Wilson was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at the City of London School, Wadham College, and Oxford, later joining the Bengal Education Department in 1887 and serving as Principal of Patna College (c. 1900–1904).
Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Yale under Whitney and in Germany, taught at Johns Hopkins, and served as Professor at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (c. 1972–2007) and later became Professor Emeritus.

Charles Schoebel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Eugène Burnouf. In 1845, he served as a schoolteacher of German at Lycée de Reims and Collège Sainte-Barbe.
Charles Swynnerton was an Indologist and historian. He studied at University College London and the University of Oxford, and he served as Headmaster of Ramsey Grammar School.

Charles Taliaferro is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College from c. 1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at McGill University and Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at the Université de Montréal, Northwestern University, and McGill University, where he served as Professor of Political Science (c. 1961–1998).

Charles Ulysse Renel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud and held posts at the universities of Caen, Franche-Comté, and Lyon.

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University and the University of Illinois System, and he held a post at Ohio University from c. 1968 to 1972.

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha. He co-founded the Asiatic Society and served as librarian for the East India Company, East India House, and the India Office Library.
Charles Willemen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker. He held an attested post as professor at Ghent University between 1999 and 2001.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin was an Iranian, Central Asian, Sinology, and Indology scholar. Educated in law at Liège, he directed Collège Saint-Quirin and became professor of Sanskrit and Oriental studies at KU Leuven/Université catholique de Louvain in 1871.

Charlotte Krause was an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. and Habilitation at Leipzig under Windisch and Hertel. She served as Hertel’s assistant at Leipzig (c. 1923–1927) and as Curator at Scindia Oriental Institute (1942–1947).
